not_covered: Anthropic released Claude 4 as two models in May 2025 to target different use cases with distinct pricing structures, positioning the family within a market where agentic coding had become the defining product category of 2025. [Source: ev-1]

The launch signaled that Anthropic was emphasizing safety and reliability for coding agents to compete effectively against OpenAI's o-series during an enterprise "agentic-coding gold rush." This strategy contributed to record API usage driven by Claude Code adoption, which helped cement Anthropic’s position as a leader in this market segment [Source: ev-1].
Anthropic released the "Claude 4" family, consisting of two models—Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4—on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1].

The launch featured distinct pricing structures to target different use cases: Opus 4 was priced at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens as the flagship model, while Sonnet 4 was priced lower at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, positioning it as a fast workhorse and developer-default coding model [Source: ev-1].
The release signaled that agentic coding had become the defining product category of 2025, with Anthropic timing the launch to coincide with the rise of Claude Code [Source: ev-1].

The strategy emphasized safety and reliability for coding agents, which contributed to record API usage and ultimately helped cement Anthropic's position as a leader in this market segment [Source: ev-1].
